resources.string: How to set up your own API key
Use your own Google Maps Platform key to find nearby restaurants online and get walking directions. Saved restaurants still appear within 500 m without a key.

You need a Google account, internet access and an active Google Cloud billing account. Google may ask for payment details during setup.\nRestaurant searches, ratings and walking routes above the applicable free allowance can incur charges. Review pricing before enabling billing.
Tap Open Google Cloud Console below.\nSign in with your Google account.\nAccept the account terms if Google asks you to.

Tap the project selector at the top of Cloud Console.
Choose New project or Create project.
Enter DineFinder as the project name, then tap Create.
Select that project from the project selector. You can also select a project you already own.
Keep this same project selected for the next steps.

Open the menu → Billing.
If you need a billing account, choose Manage billing accounts → Create account and complete Google’s payment setup.
Return to your project’s Billing page.
Choose Link a billing account and select your active account.
If the project already has an active linked account, continue to step 4.

Open the menu → APIs & Services → Library.
Search for Places API (New), open it and tap Enable.
Repeat for Routes API in the same project.
If an API shows Manage instead, it is already enabled.
Places finds restaurants and their available details; Routes provides walking directions.

Open APIs & Services → Credentials.
Tap Create credentials → API key.
A dialog shows your new key. Copy it, then tap Close.
Keep the key private and restrict it in step 6 before using it.

On Credentials, open the key you just created.
Under Application restrictions, choose Android apps → Add.
Enter the app package name and signing SHA-1. Open App restriction help below to find these details.
Under API restrictions, choose Restrict key and select Places API (New) and Routes API.
Tap Save. Keep the app and API restrictions enabled.

Copy your API key from Cloud Console → Credentials.
Return to DineFinder → Profile → Settings → Google Maps API.
Paste only the key text into API key, then tap Save API key.
You should see API key saved. This stores the key on your device; Google checks it when you search for restaurants or request a route.
Find a restaurant and try directions

Wait a few minutes for Cloud changes to apply, and keep internet and location on.
On Home, tap Scan for Restaurant. Allow camera and precise location access.
Turn toward restaurants within 500 m. Matching places appear as camera markers when they are in view.
Tap a marker to see its type, rating and halal status, then tap Get directions.
A successful route request shows Walking route loaded. Follow the main walking instruction; the smaller Then instruction shows the turn ahead. The moving 3D pointer leads along your current walking path toward the next junction. Pan or tilt your phone to follow it. If the path is outside the view, the pointer stays at the screen edge to show which way to move the camera. Near a turn, the instruction can name that turn while the pointer still leads to the junction first. It is a guide and is not attached to the physical road.
Compatible phones may offer an optional Google Play Services for AR installation or update. You can decline and use the camera and phone orientation sensors instead. No additional API key setup is needed. If an error appears, use the tips below.
Walking routes can omit sidewalks or pedestrian paths. Check your surroundings and use safe paths.

DineFinder’s package name is com.example.dinefinder.
Ask the app provider or developer for the signing SHA-1 of the exact DineFinder build installed on your phone. Enter these two values in Cloud Console’s Android apps restriction.

If you build the app yourself:
Open the project in Android Studio → Terminal.
Run bash ./gradlew :app:signingReport (Windows: gradlew.bat :app:signingReport).
Use the SHA-1 for the debug or release variant installed on your phone.

For a Play Store build:
Use Play Console → App integrity → App signing and copy the App signing key certificate SHA-1. Use the app-signing certificate, which can differ from the upload certificate.

Debug, release and Play Store builds can use different certificates. A fingerprint from another build will not match your installed app.

Monitor Places and Routes usage in your Cloud project. Restaurant ratings can add charges beyond the initial search. Set suitable request quotas and billing alerts. Alerts-only budgets do not automatically cap spending. Removing the key stops new online restaurant and route requests in DineFinder; saved restaurants remain available. Delete or restrict the key in Cloud Console to control access elsewhere.
If restaurants or routes do not load

Check the pasted key and confirm Places API (New) and Routes API are both allowed in the same Cloud project. Recheck the Android app details from step 6 and App restriction help. Keep the restrictions enabled.
Enable Places API (New) and Routes API in the key’s project and check its linked billing account. Wait a few minutes after changing Cloud settings, then retry.
Check API usage and quotas in Cloud Console. Wait for the quota to reset, or review pricing before increasing it.
No camera markers or walking route

Check camera and precise location permission, location services and compass accuracy. Face a restaurant within 500 m. Google restaurant lookup needs internet and a configured key; saved places work without them. A walking route may be unavailable in some areas.\nThe moving 3D pointer needs a usable walking path, fresh GPS, a live camera and reliable heading. It follows your walking route and responds as you pan or tilt the phone. A pointer at the edge means the path is outside the camera view. Read the walking instructions for when to turn.\nIf AR tracking pauses, the pointer hides until tracking recovers. Keep the camera steady and face a well-lit area. Unsupported phones, or declining the optional AR installation, use camera and orientation sensors instead. Calibrate the compass if the direction is unreliable. No extra Cloud API or key is required.
